description: Johann Sebastian Bach, cantor in Leipzig, took fugue and counterpoint to their peak and became the architect of the Baroque.

hero.hook: A Leipzig cantor builds the sound cathedral of the West.

blocks.text: **Johann Sebastian Bach** (**1685**-**1750**) is often considered the pinnacle of Western music. Architect of sounds, he brings to perfection the art of **fugue** and : several independent melodic lines that intertwine. [[Counterpoint and fugue]]
His life is not that of a court star. It is that of a genius craftsman, at the service of the Church and princes, whose work would only be fully rediscovered in the 19th century.

The **baroque** era goes from approximately **1600** to Bach's death. She likes contrast, movement, ornament. **Vivaldi** in Italy, **Handel** in Germany then in England, dominate the landscape. Music serves three missions: the church (organ and sacred song), the princes' bedroom, and the stage (opera).

Bach did not write an opera, but he injected lyrical drama into his Passions and oratorios. It synthesizes French measure, Italian lyricism and German rigor. For him, music reflects a divine order, not just pleasure.
In 1717 in Weimar, Bach spent a month in prison for having insisted too strongly on resigning: the duke refused to let him leave for Köthen.

Born in **Eisenach** in **1685** into a dynasty of musicians, Bach settled in **1723** in **Leipzig** as  of the St. Thomas Church. Overwhelming load: a new  almost every week, plus teaching . [[cantor]] [[cantata]] [[Thomasschule]]

blocks.text: It is estimated that approximately **300** cantatas were composed, of which some **200** have reached us. He has **20** children from two marriages; **Carl Philipp Emanuel** and **Johann Christian** became major composers themselves. In the evening, he directs the , an ensemble for which he writes concertos and secular suites. [[Collegium Musicum]]
At the end of his life, undergoing eye surgery by traveling surgeon John Taylor, Bach became blind shortly before dying.

blocks.text: With the , a tuning system that unifies intervals, Bach proves that a keyboard can play in all keys. *The Well-Tempered Keyboard* (48 preludes and fugues) opens the way to modern music. His fugue superimposes a theme taken up by several voices: mathematical architecture. [[Equal temperament]]

blocks.caption: The Well-Tempered Keyboard: all the tones on a single keyboard.

blocks.text: When he died, fashion preferred the lighter . Bach seems “gothic”. In **1829**, the young **Felix Mendelssohn** conducted the *St. Matthew Passion* in Berlin: beginning of the “Bach Renaissance”. Without him, hundreds of scores could have disappeared. [[style galant]]
Mendelssohn joked: it was necessary for a converted Jew and an actor (his friend Devrient) to return to the world the greatest masterpiece of Christian music.

blocks.text: A fervent Lutheran, Bach often signed **SDG** (*Soli Deo Gloria*: to God alone the glory). He plays with the  and codes his name (B-A-C-H) in notes. In **1977**, NASA placed several of his works on the  of the Voyager probes: humanity's sound embassy to space. [[numerology]] [[Golden Record]]
